Merged the duplicates into the canonical policy and locked the retired copies read-only with a pointer to the survivor.
The consolidation dashboard can be retired too, but archive the burn-down panel somewhere first; it is a nice record of the migration actually finishing.
Archived the burn-down panel into the migrations folder and retired the rest of the consolidation dashboard.
Can you also sweep the alert annotations for links to the old paging service? Anything that still deep-links there will break when it is decommissioned next month.
Swept the annotations and rewrote the deep links to the new paging service; the decommission checklist now shows zero inbound references from alerting.
The oncall shadow program needs its schedule refreshed as well; two of the listed shadows rotated teams during the consolidation.
Refreshed the shadow schedule with two replacements and confirmed both have paging access in the new service.
Finally, make sure the consolidation retro captures the fanout sizing discussion; people keep relitigating it from memory and the numbers deserve a written home.
Added a fanout sizing section to the retro doc summarizing the discussion and linking the load test results that settled it.
A few stragglers too. The paging test rotation that ran during the consolidation is still sending its weekly synthetic page to the old service; retarget it before someone treats a synthetic as real.
Retargeted the synthetic page at the new service and labelled it clearly as synthetic in the alert body so a half-awake responder cannot mistake it.
The escalation training doc for new oncallers predates the consolidation as well; it walks through screenshots of the old service and will just confuse the next cohort.
Rewrote the training doc against the new service with fresh screenshots, and the next cohort's session is already booked to use it.
And confirm the old paging service's data export completed before the decommission date; the compliance folks want the acknowledgement trail preserved.
The export completed and the acknowledgement trail is archived in the compliance bucket with a retention hold; I sent the confirmation to the compliance folks.
